name: Leona Valley

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Nebbiolo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Merlot is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Zinfandel is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: River deposits are a mix of gravel, sand and silt. They are often fertile, so vines can grow vigorously.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
